primary_test.method: Two-sided model-based OLS t test with n-p residual degrees of freedom.
primary_test.parameter: Adjusted linear-model mean score difference per 0.1 mm greater left thickness at the same age, recorded sex and education.
primary_test.decision_rule: Use the registered model-based test for the primary decision; report HC3 alongside it without selecting a covariance method by p-value.
primary_test.interpretation: The registered primary test does not reject a zero adjusted thickness coefficient at alpha=0.05. Interpret the estimate and both intervals in correct responses per 0.1 mm. Non-rejection does not establish no association or practical equivalence; no equivalence margin has been supplied. The result remains conditional on the model and sampling assumptions, with residual and influence review pending.

methods.estimator: Ordinary least squares with an intercept, equal participant weights and no regularization.
methods.numerics: Use a numerically stable QR/SVD least-squares solution; check full column rank before interpretation, rather than solving through an explicitly inverted normal equation.
methods.model_based_covariance: s^2 (X'X)^(-1), with s^2 = SSE/(n-p) and p including the intercept.
methods.coefficient_intervals: Individual two-sided 95% Student t intervals, estimate +/- t(0.975,n-p) SE. Exact t calibration requires the classical independent, homoskedastic normal-error linear model; otherwise qualifications are required.

hc3_companion.role: Prespecified companion coefficient uncertainty, reported alongside the model-based results regardless of diagnostic significance; never choose whichever gives a smaller p-value.
hc3_companion.reference_distribution: Use t with n-p degrees of freedom as an explicit finite-sample convention; HC3 interval/test calibration is approximate, not exact normal-theory t inference.
hc3_companion.limit: HC3 addresses coefficient covariance under heteroskedasticity; it does not correct nonlinearity, dependence, selection bias or source imputation uncertainty and does not supply a heteroskedastic individual prediction interval.

assumptions: Independent participant observations under the sampling model.
An adequate additive linear conditional-mean specification over the observed predictor support.
A full-rank design matrix and finite error variance.
Constant conditional error variance for model-based SEs and classical individual prediction intervals; normal errors for exact t-based calibration.
methods.interval_scope: Individual coefficient intervals; not simultaneous intervals or new-observation prediction intervals.
methods.p_value: Under the relevant zero-coefficient null and test assumptions, the p-value is the tail probability of a t statistic at least as far from zero as observed. It is not the probability that the null is true.
methods.numeric_tail: A computed coefficient p-value of zero is flagged as numerical underflow, not interpreted as a literal zero probability.

testing_policy.multiplicity: One primary Phase 4 coefficient test at alpha 0.05. Secondary and companion p-values are explicitly nominal; no familywise guarantee across coefficients, methods or phases is claimed. The separate completed Phase 3 Holm family remains unchanged.
testing_policy.other_coefficients: Report estimates, SEs, t statistics, nominal p-values and individual intervals as supporting model descriptions. Do not make a collection of unadjusted significance claims.
testing_policy.scope: The integrated thickness test is primary. All other coefficient p-values and HC3 companions are nominal supporting summaries; no familywise guarantee across them is claimed.

validation.limit: Computational agreement does not validate the conditional mean, residual distribution, participant independence or sampling frame.

sampling_and_preparation.unit: One participant with the single supplied UDS record and the single supplied MRI record, joined one-to-one on NACCID.
sampling_and_preparation.target: The source population represented by this teaching extract, conditional on model_normal eligibility and the sampling/model assumptions; no claim of representativeness for all NACC participants.
sampling_and_preparation.independence: One supplied row per ID is verified; independence across people remains a modeling assumption.
sampling_and_preparation.selection: Random selection is reported, but its sampling frame, selection probabilities and source selection eligibility are undocumented.
sampling_and_preparation.source_preparation: The source preparation and imputation methods and value-level masks are unknown. Treat the supplied values as fixed inputs; this analysis cannot propagate additional imputation/preparation uncertainty.

visit_and_scan_timing.record_rule: Use the single supplied record per participant; no within-person visit selection is possible or performed.
visit_and_scan_timing.temporal_proximity: Unverifiable from the supplied files; do not assert baseline, first visit, nearest scan or contemporaneous measurements.
visit_and_scan_timing.track_c5_status: Participant-level input structure is documented. Temporal proximity remains unverified and would require authoritative metadata or course-team clarification.

sampling_and_preparation.scan_quality: Finite positive thickness establishes numerical usability, not scan-level quality control.

limitations.response_scale: A task score is not a diagnosis or a calibrated clinical change. The count is analyzed with OLS as a conditional-mean approximation; inspect residuals and predictions against its scale.
limitations.causality: An observational association under the stated functional form and assumptions; neither a within-person change nor a causal effect.
limitations.functional_form: If the additive linear mean is inadequate, qualify this constant-slope summary and report any diagnostic extension separately.
limitations.uncertainty: Classical t calibration requires its error assumptions. HC3 t calibration is approximate and does not correct dependence, nonlinearity, selection or source-imputation uncertainty.
limitations.fit: All fit metrics are in-sample summaries, not externally validated predictive accuracy or a basis for choosing a causal model.
